note: The meetings tools whose MCP surface is exactly one meeting-api route: each is called back through the gateway, which fronts every meetings route at the same path (core/meetings/routes.v1.json, mcp_reentry), carrying the identity it signed. The other eighteen meetings tools are still the MCP edge's own (core/meetings/services/mcp/src/vexa_mcp/app.py), because each does work a forward cannot: parse_meeting_link and report_issue are edge logic; request_meeting_bot parses the link and answers a repeat request with the existing meeting; update_bot_config, stop_bot, get_meeting_chat, speak_in_meeting and get_meeting_participants default the platform, refuse an unknown one and take the deprecated meeting_platform/meeting_id aliases; list_meetings, get_meeting_transcript, search_transcripts, annotate_meeting and list_recordings validate a filter, page with since_index, trim an echo or rename meeting_db_id to the REST meeting_id; get_meeting and delete_meeting address the row as meeting_db_id while the REST route names it meeting_id (a retired name on any tool input), and delete_meeting and speak_in_meeting hold the asked_by_a_human gate. The three bot-account tools (ADR-0049) are the edge's too: browser_session_open adds the ui_action a client opens the live sign-in view from, bot_account_verify takes the account id in a validated body and names it in the path, and bot_accounts_list (a plain GET /bot-accounts) stays beside them. meeting-api's require_person still refuses a delete from a worker whose person is not present.
